summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update6.json → valid=true). Adversarial check aimed at refuting the newly recorded A1 progress finding (repeating InstallSnapshot) from the retained tests, reading their premises rather than their names. Result: no retained expectation covers the finding's premise. Both snapshot-to-follower tests (raft_test.go:1598-1637, 1640-1689) manufacture the need for a snapshot by disconnecting a follower before the leader advances, so the follower's last index stays far below the snapshot index and the receiver takes the safe branch where getLastEntry/getLastIndex prefer the snapshot term and accept PrevLogEntry equal to the snapshot index; both then only assert convergence after reconnect. They also set TrailingLogs=10, i.e. the leader's log is compacted right above its snapshot, which isolates the deciding factor as the follower's cached last index — the one thing the tests never make exceed the snapshot index, while the leader always ships its newest snapshot (replication.go:299-320). Recorded as one Fact (what the tests fix and how they set it up) and an 'explained' interpretation that keeps the counterevidence prominent: the tests do show the snapshot path works whenever the cached position is below the snapshot index and with a compacted leader, so the cycle cannot be widened to snapshot installs in general; the index-ahead premise remains a stated construction (a follower holding a superseded leader's uncommitted suffix longer than the new leader's snapshot index, diverging at or below it) rather than an observation, and no execution was performed. This closes the loop on the A1 finding without weakening it: requirement side unchanged, and the would-be refutation is removed while the reachability argument stays explicitly conditional.
